We have deployed enterprise LLM tooling organisation-wide (Claude Enterprise) across all teams, but lack dedicated resource to drive adoption, govern use, and deliver production automations. This hire owns the AI adoption and automation delivery mandate. This is primarily an AI adoption and automation delivery role—not a data engineering role.

The engineer will work closely with Operations, Finance, Compliance, and Technology teams to identify automation opportunities, build production-grade solutions, and ensure every deployment is safe, governed, and measurable.

Data pipeline engineering and Snowflake modelling sit with the data engineering team; this role uses the data platform as a consumer and integration point. The tech stack includes Azure, Power Automate, Python, the Claude API, and Microsoft 365 integrations.

The engineer operates within the AI governance framework owned by Compliance, Risk, and the DPO, contributing technical evidence and controls, not setting policy. This role can be hybrid at our office in Portimao or fully remote across Portugal.

Key Responsibilities AI Adoption & Use-Case Delivery Work with business stakeholders across Operations, Finance, and Technology to identify, prioritise, and scope AI and automation use cases Maintain and manage the AI use-case register, including intake, prioritisation, status tracking, and outcomes measurement Drive adoption of deployed AI tools (Claude Enterprise and equivalents) — structured rollout, training, and usage measurement by function Stay current on enterprise LLM and AI tooling developments; advise the Data & AI Lead on relevant capabilities Automation Engineering Design and build production-grade automations using Power Automate, Python, and API integrations, targeting operational workflows across payments, FX, treasury, onboarding, and internal operations Build and maintain automated workflows and AI pipelines with human-in-the-loop controls, escalation paths, and audit trails Integrate LLM workflows with internal systems and third-party APIs using the Claude API or equivalent enterprise LLM APIs; Document all automations with clear operational runbooks; ensure solutions are maintainable by others Production Controls & Governance Apply production engineering standards to all AI deployments: secrets management, prompt and model versioning, evaluation datasets, output quality thresholds, and observability Implement cost monitoring and usage controls for LLM API consumption Build and maintain rollback and kill-switch mechanisms for all production AI workflows Apply personal data minimisation principles — no personal data in prompts unless explicitly reviewed and approved Produce the technical input for vendor, security, privacy, and data-residency assessments for any new AI tool or integration, working with the relevant control functions Operate within the AI governance framework; provide technical evidence and control documentation to Compliance, Risk, Security, and the DPO as required Maintain awareness of AI regulatory developments, including the EU AI Act timetable, and flag implications to the Data & AI Lead and Compliance SOP & Process Redesign Work with Operations to review existing SOPs and identify where automation can reduce manual effort, error risk, or processing time Where automation is not yet appropriate, document improved manual processes that are automation-ready Measure and report on automation impact — hours saved, error reduction, throughput improvements Requirements Essential 3–6 years of hands-on software or automation engineering experience Proficiency in Python (e.g. scripting, API integration, workflow automation) Practical experience building with enterprise LLM APIs, such as Claude API, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or equivalent Experience with Power Automate or equivalent low-code/no-code automation platforms in a production context Ability to gather requirements from non-technical stakeholders and translate into working solutions Understanding of production controls: secrets management, versioning, observability, error handling, and rollback Strong written English (e.g. documentation, runbooks, and stakeholder communication) Preferred Experience with agentic AI patterns and multi-step LLM workflows with human oversight Background in financial services, payments, or another regulated sector Familiarity with Azure services used as integration and compute infrastructure Experience with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem as an integration target (Graph API, Teams, SharePoint) Awareness of AI governance frameworks and practical privacy controls for LLM deployments Benefits at VFX We offer more than just perks—we offer ownership.

ABOUT US Storyteller is a high-growth B2B SaaS platform that enables companies to add Stories experiences to their own apps and websites. Stories help our clients increase engagement, retention and revenue.

Our platform combines SDKs, publishing tools, analytics and advertising support so enterprise customers can launch a complete Stories experience quickly. We work with major sports and media brands, and the experiences we power are used by large audiences around the world. About the Role This is an AI-native quality engineering role.

You will use AI as a core part of how you investigate software, build automated tests, understand unfamiliar code, diagnose failures and make changes. Your work will span the quality of SDK behaviour and the integration between Storyteller SDKs, platform services and APIs.

Storyteller has SDKs across iOS, Android, Web, tvOS, Fire TV, Android TV and Roku. The role will initially focus on iOS and Android, with opportunities to contribute across the wider SDK portfolio over time.

This is a hands-on engineering role, but not a separate QA gatekeeping function: You’ll use AI coding agents and related tools to explore the SDK codebases, understand behaviour and accelerate quality work. You’ll care about tests that protect important behaviour and run in real development and release workflows.

You’ll use product, technical, integration and release risk to identify the highest-value quality improvements. You will work as a senior individual contributor inside the Storyteller team. Quality belongs to the whole team, and you will work directly with builders and product owners throughout the product and engineering lifecycle.

Success is measured by the confidence and useful evidence the work gives the team. RESPONSIBILITIES Use AI coding agents and related tools to explore the SDK codebases, understand behaviour and accelerate quality work. Use product, technical, integration and release risk to identify the highest-value quality improvements.

Design, build and maintain useful unit and component tests for SDK behaviour. Design, build and maintain integration tests covering SDK interaction with Storyteller services and APIs. Put automated tests into active CI and release workflows, with failures that are clear and actionable.

Prove that tests detect meaningful breakage rather than merely producing passing output. Investigate bugs using code, logs, APIs, test results and product behaviour. Where appropriate, follow a well-understood issue through to a bounded production fix. Work with builders to improve testability and prevent repeated classes of defects.

Turn repeated investigation or testing work into reusable AI workflows, tools, checks or test assets. Communicate clearly in Slack and other team systems: state the evidence, impact, current understanding, owner and next action.

Contribute useful AI-assisted engineering practices to the wider SDK team while remaining primarily accountable for quality outcomes. Contribute to tvOS, Android TV, Fire TV, Web and Roku as the role's scope expands.

What Good Looks Like  You will be succeeding when:  Important SDK behaviours have dependable automated protection;  Useful quality improvements land incrementally and are easy for the team to adopt;  SDK-to-platform integration failures are detected early and are easy to diagnose;  Tests run reliably in the workflows the team actually uses;  Test failures give the team enough information to act;  Well-understood defects are followed through to an appropriate fix or clear handover;  Repeated quality problems become better tests, tooling or product changes;  Automation and risk-based exploration provide evidence proportionate to the change;  Your communication makes quality risks and next actions easy to understand;  And the Storyteller team becomes more capable with AI because of practical workflows you have demonstrated through the work.

QUALIFICATIONS What we’re looking for AI-native execution – You use AI to do substantive technical work, not only to write or summarise. You can give an agent useful context, break down an ambiguous problem, inspect its work, redirect it when necessary and keep going when the first approach fails.

Quality and validation judgment – You can decide what is worth testing, recognise superficial tests and demonstrate that an automated test provides real protection. You think about false confidence, false positives, brittle tests, maintainability and failure diagnosis.

Agency and ownership – You can take an ambiguous quality risk, investigate it, gather evidence, choose a sensible next step and move the work towards a useful outcome. Technical comfort – You are comfortable working with repositories, code, APIs, CI, logs, command-line tools and automated test frameworks.

You can understand and challenge AI-generated code well enough to validate and land it safely. Problem solving and systems thinking – You distinguish symptoms from root causes. When a problem repeats, you look for a reusable test, tool, check or workflow instead of treating every occurrence as a new manual task.

Clear communication – You communicate concisely and directly. You make evidence, impact, uncertainty, ownership and next actions visible without requiring someone else to reconstruct the situation. Learning velocity – You are curious and can become effective in unfamiliar products, codebases and tools quickly.

You change your approach when the evidence shows that it is not working. You do not need to be able to write Swift or Kotlin expertly without AI assistance, have deep experience across every Storyteller SDK platform, have held a traditional QA, test-automation or SDET title, or have managed a separate QA team.

Nice to have Experience with mobile applications or SDKs. Experience with Swift or Kotlin. Experience with API integration. Experience with automated testing or test frameworks.

These may help you become effective faster, but demonstrated AI-native execution, quality judgment and validation discipline matter more than matching a conventional technology checklist. Is this You? This role will likely suit you if: You can take an ambiguous quality risk from signal to outcome with limited supervision.

You can frame the problem, direct AI and other tools effectively, and choose a practical testing or investigation approach. You validate output rigorously, communicate what you found and land useful work. You improve the system for the next occurrence rather than treating every problem as a one-off.

You are comfortable being accountable for quality outcomes while quality remains a shared responsibility across the team. It probably isn’t right for you if: You want AI to produce technical work that you do not need to understand, explain or validate.

You prefer to wait for fully defined instructions rather than investigate ambiguous risks and choose a sensible next step. You are looking for a separate QA gatekeeping role rather than working directly with builders and product owners throughout the lifecycle. RECRUITMENT PROCESS We keep the process straightforward and respectful of your time.  1.

Hiring Manager Conversation (20–30 mins)  A short call to get to know you, share more about Storyteller and the QA Engineer role, and answer your questions. There is no technical exercise at this stage. We’ll both aim to decide whether it makes sense to go deeper 2.

Paid Take-home Task (~60 mins)  A small, focused quality-engineering task that you can complete in your own time. We compensate you for completing it, regardless of the outcome. You’re welcome to use AI tools.

We’re interested in how you investigate unfamiliar software, identify meaningful risks, validate your work and explain your decisions—not how much code you can write from memory. 3.

Review and CTO Interview (60–75 mins)  We’ll review your submission together and discuss how you approached the task, what you tested, how you verified the results and any risks or limitations you identified.

You’ll also meet Dave, our CTO, and talk about how you investigate quality issues, use tools such as AI, communicate your findings and work with engineers to improve software quality. And that’s it. Delta operates three AI products used by live traders: a customer support chatbot, an API Copilot that generates and executes trading scripts, and an MCP server. This role owns the quality of those products and is responsible for measuring it objectively.
Testing probabilistic systems differs fundamentally from testing deterministic ones. The same input produces different output on every run, an incorrect answer can be entirely fluent, and a prompt change in one flow can degrade another without any visible signal. The core of this role is establishing what correct means for these systems, building the datasets and scoring that measure it, and operating the release gate that prevents a regression from reaching customers.
This is an emerging discipline with no established playbook. We are defining the methodology as we build it, and the role carries a high degree of autonomy and ownership.
🔬 What Sets This Role Apart
Most QA roles that mention AI mean using AI to do testing faster: generating test cases from a PRD, healing flaky selectors, exploring an app with an agent. Those are useful and we do them.
This role is the other thing. The system under test is itself an AI, and the hard problem is deciding whether its output is correct when the same question produces a different answer every time and a wrong answer reads as convincingly as a right one. That means building evaluation datasets, defining what correct looks like, scoring against it, and defending a number that decides whether a release ships.
If you have spent time on the second problem, this role is built for you.

Build and maintain golden datasets for our AI products, trace mined from production or generated, and verified against a documented source of truth.
Design layered scoring for AI outputs: deterministic rules where behaviour can be asserted, and model-graded evaluation where it cannot.
Manage evaluation runs end to end: schedule and execute them against release candidates, compare results against prior baselines, and triage failures into product defects, incorrect expectations, and platform issues.
Own and operate the release gate that determines whether a prompt or model change is approved for production.
Identify failure modes ahead of customers, including hallucination, incorrect tool selection, loss of context across conversation turns, and PII exposure.
Investigate production traces to distinguish retrieval failures from generation failures from tool failures.
Convert findings into actionable engineering evidence and into permanent regression coverage.
Define and report quality metrics for AI surfaces, and drive improvement against them.
